title: Produce direct Unity and Godot GLB import evidence for accepted Forge exports
description: Produce direct Unity and Godot GLB import evidence for the reload-verified reference GLB set, beyond the pinned Three.js GLTFLoader audit, using a versioned per-engine evidence contract that records importer version, glTF-validator report, node/material/scale/bounds findings, and explicit Pass/Fail/Not-Assessed status; refresh the capability catalog so Unity and Godot are no longer Not Assessed.
deviation_notes: New track retires the Open Medium tech-debt item 'External game-engine compatibility remains unassessed - Three.js GLTFLoader passes; Unity, Godot, and gameplay-runtime scale/material behavior still need direct evidence.' GLB exports are mechanically accepted (reload-verified), so this assessment is not blocked by the pending visual acceptance gates. Unity and Godot remain out of scope as backends; they are assessed only as import targets. If an engine importer is unavailable on the host, the result is explicitly Not-Assessed (fail-closed honesty) rather than inferred. This track must not modify measure/automation-supervisor.py.

sprint.goal: Move Unity and Godot GLB compatibility from Not Assessed to assessed with direct importer evidence, without making any engine a backend.
